outcome: Complications (wound infection, febrile morbidity, paralytic ileus, secondary hemorrhage)
cohort: The study included 70 women with symptomatic uterine fibroids, divided into two groups: those who underwent cesarean myomectomy and those who underwent interval myomectomy at a tertiary care hospital.
finding: Cesarean myomectomy was associated with significantly longer operative time, higher blood loss, greater postoperative hemoglobin drop, and a longer hospital stay compared to interval myomectomy, but without a significant increase in major complications.
mod_finding: Cesarean myomectomy, when performed during childbirth, was associated with greater operative time, blood loss, and longer hospital stay compared to interval myomectomy, but did not significantly increase major complications.
